name: Kildin Sami

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Kildin Saami (kild1236).

notes: Research. Kildin Sami is a Kola (Eastern) Saami language of the Uralic family, written in an extended Cyrillic alphabet (Kert 1971 orthography, revised 1980s). The map covers the base Cyrillic letters plus the language-specific graphemes: Ӈ (velar nasal), the voiceless-sonorant letters Ӆ Ӎ Ӊ Ҏ, the voiceless glide Ҋ, and Һ (marking preaspiration). Iotated Е Ё Ю Я are given their glide+vowel reading. Vowel length is written with a combining macron over the base vowel letter (а̄ э̄ ы̄ о̄ я̄ ю̄ е̄) or, for и/у, with the dedicated precomposed letters Ӣ/Ӯ; both are modelled as long vowels here (Kert 1971), which is the largest single source of the pre-upgrade PER gap. Word stress is fixed on the first syllable (Kert 1971). Palatalization written with Ь or Ҍ is encoded. Ь and ҍ both map to ʲ, which the engine composes onto the consonant before them, so no consonant-plus-sign key is needed for the compositional cases. Kildin Sami contrasts plain, half-palatalized and palatal consonants, so the sign is a segmental instruction rather than a lexical diacritic; the Kola Saami Documentation Project gives the minimal triple манн /manː/ 'moon', маннҍ /manːʲ/ 'egg', маннь /maɲː/ 'daughter-in-law', which is why ⟨нҍ⟩ composes to nʲ while ⟨нь⟩ is the palatal nasal ɲ. Four keys earn a slot because their value is not the concatenation of their parts: ⟨ль⟩ ʎ, ⟨сь⟩ ɕ, ⟨хь⟩ ç and ⟨нь⟩ ɲ, the palatal segments the majority of the shipped gold writes for those four letters (ʎ in 85 occurrences against lʲ in 43; ɕ in 75 against sʲ in 23; ç in 39 against xʲ in 6; ɲ in 11 against nʲ in 0). ҍ is not in that set: it is the half-palatalization sign and keeps the plain ʲ reading. Ъ is left unencoded as the empty string: it appears in only a handful of sign occurrences, the two gold sets do not agree on a reading, and in ⟨куллъе⟩ it separates rather than palatalizes. Palatalization does not spread rightward across a cluster: of 150 sign-plus-consonant contexts in the WikiPron gold only 75 write the following consonant as palatalized, and the NorthEuraLex gold writes 5 of 209. The two gold sets differ in how much of this they transcribe. NorthEuraLex writes the palatal segments but leaves secondary palatalization off labials, velars and liquids (0 of 17 ⟨вь⟩, 0 of 9 ⟨пь⟩, 2 of 47 ⟨рь⟩, 8 of 31 ⟨кь⟩), so encoding the sign raises its exact-match error even though it lowers its PER.
